g.text: Isolation valve, technology to be selected
HOLD – decision needed, see hold list
Draft generated from the specification 'Cahier des Charges P&ID Consolidé' – not for construction.
Orange items are additions proposed by the project rules (valves, instruments, tags, line numbers); approval is per rule,
Line numbers are <service code>-<sequence>. Sizes and piping classes are not given in the specification and are not
Valve failure positions, design pressures, relief devices, instrument ranges and nozzle sizes are not given and are not
Future heat pumps PAC 3A/3B are shown dashed and unconnected (LifeCyclePhase = Future).
Operating modes (normal, emergency exchangers, ultimate) are realised with the isolation valves shown; see the
Emergency exchangers ECH-030..032 – parallel or series?
Drawn: Parallel branch of the cooling-water loop, beside the heat-pump evaporators. Question: Confirm parallel
arrangement and the well-water path in Normal mode.
Drawn: 2A condenser feeds the 2B evaporator through the 55/50 °C internal loop; only 2B delivers 85/105 °C to RCUA.
Circulation pumps of the fermenter leg and hot-water loops
Drawn: Only P-033..035 (TK-002 outlet). No other pump drawn – the specification names none. Question: Where are the
circulation pumps of the fermenter leg and of the hot-water loops?
RCUA buffer – one tank or one per temperature level?
Drawn: One RCUA buffer tank (85/105 °C). Question: One RCUA tank or one per temperature level?
Spill valves 8→4 and 4→1 bar – control philosophy
Drawn: Control valves with manifolds, no control loop (variable, setpoint and fail position not given). Question: Control
Flash tank – liquid destination and CMV staging
Drawn: Flash vapour → CMV stages 1-2-3 in series; 70 °C liquid outlet left open. Question: Flash-tank liquid destination
Air-preheating coil – 85 °C limit on a 90 °C header
Drawn: One coil (TGE example) fed directly from the 90/70 °C header; no tempering arrangement. Question: How is the
85 °C inlet limit achieved, and how many coils are needed?
Thermal degasser – 4 bar or 1 bar steam?
Drawn: Steam inlet left unconnected. Question: Select 4 bar or 1 bar for the degasser.
Drawn: Hot side left open. Question: Heating medium of the make-up heater.
LPF tank heating loops – pump and steam supply
Drawn: Plate exchangers on the tank loops; retained steam exchangers on standby with open steam/condensate
Ultimate mode – well-water feed to the fermenters
Drawn: Only the post-fermenter discharge to DARSE is drawn.
Hot-water networks – local steam back-up equipment
Drawn: Placeholder battery-limit flags for the 105 °C supply and 85 °C return.
Valve technology of the generic valves
Drawn: Generic valve symbol, DEXPI CustomOperatedValve 'technology to be selected'. Question: Select the valve
DATA TO BE COMPLETED ON DATASHEETS (NOT HOLDS)
Equipment tags are given only for P-030..035, ECH-030..032, TK-001/002, K3/MESSO/GEA and the LPF tanks
No nozzle numbers or nozzle sizes are given for any equipment (except DN50 on the TGE coil)
No design pressures, relief devices/sizing, safety thresholds (other than 7.5 bar eff.), valve failure positions, material
classes or instrument ranges are giv…
PAC 3A/3B are future equipment with no capacity, regime or connection data
Failure position (fail open / close / retain) of the control valves is not specified and was not assumed
Measuring ranges and alarm/trip settings of the generated instruments are not specified and were not assumed
Nozzles added for drain, vent and level tapping have no nozzle number and no size
Draft generated from the specification – issued for engineering review
